options.text: A circle with centre $F$, because every pencil point stays the same distance from $F$.
A circle with centre at the pencil tip, not at $F$.
A straight line segment whose length is the compass opening.
The fixed length is the centre, and $F$ is the radius.

stem:
Falguni opens a compass to a fixed length, keeps the metal point fixed at $F$, and moves only the pencil.

What path does the pencil draw?

teacher.key_rationale: Fixed point F and fixed opening make every pencil position equidistant from F, so the path is a circle centred at F. Putting the centre at the pencil reverses centre and moving point. A straight segment conflates a different construction. Swapping the names centre and radius substitutes terms.
